goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weeder check` judges a diff and may block; `weeder scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weeder guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weeder bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose — only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
The classification of blocked commits into true positive, acceptable and false positive is the number weeder ships on, so it is not the builder's word. A second party on a different provider re-classifies a random sample of at least twenty blocked commits from `docs/calibration-2026-09.md` and at least twenty cases from the recall sample, blind to the first classification, and writes `docs/calibration-audit-2026-09.md`. Agreement at or above 90 percent on each sample stands; below it, the classification is untrusted and redone before anything ships.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/calibration-audit.tend2.html) is your full context — read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) the seal covers the judged content alone: a case packet carries the rule ids, each finding's level, path and line, and the commit's hunks, and no finding sentence, so the wording a message teaches can change without a re-seal; `cargo xtask audit-packet` writes that shape, the fairness and transcript evidence hold it, and the packets are regenerated under the renamed token with forty fresh blind reads and the sighted run recorded on a fresh seed by `scripts/audit/blind-run.sh` and `scripts/audit/sighted-run.sh` on opencode with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (`opencode run --model … --format json`, the packet on stdin, the raw event stream kept as each session's record and refused if it shows a tool part), every audit file and every session record naming the provider and the model since this population differs from the earlier seals', every answer opening with its packet's hash, and the agreement recomputed · evidence expected at: scripts/check/audit-fairness.sh

## Definition of done — verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/calibration-audit.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload ac4eb87d86f2 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 shaped from cape-town's binding checks; the owner may take the auditor's seat instead of a second provider, and the script does not care which
- 2026-09-06 conductor: the pleach running these nodes stages every path the Write and Edit tools touched, wherever it is. A path outside this worktree (under `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp`) makes the collector ask git about a file it cannot see, which kills the delivery and removes the worktree (dogfood P8, P11); `.loop-scratch/` is collected and judged by the hygiene gate (P10). So: never use the Write or Edit tool outside this worktree; write scratch outside it only through the shell; leave `.loop-scratch/` empty before you finish; and never leave a credential-shaped string, even a quoted one, in a file that will be collected
- 2026-09-06 built by pleach node `calibration-audit` (codex worker, claude audit), both checks stamped, landed through `pleach land`. `docs/calibration-audit-2026-09.md` re-grades twenty blocked commits and twenty recall cases drawn by SHA-256 over a seed, and agrees with the builder's classification on every one of both samples; `scripts/check/calibration-agreement.sh` redraws the sample and recomputes the agreement. Total agreement is a strong result and a reason to look at the draw: the sample comes from the calibration file's own tables, where the builder's class sits beside the commit, so the auditor could read it before judging. A later audit should hand the auditor the diffs and nothing else
- 2026-09-06 cape-town, on the anchoring caveat: the unqualified verdict stands today on the sighted audit, and a blind one is what makes it stand tomorrow. Shaped above: the auditor receives diffs and rule ids only, never the class, on a fresh seed, same 90 percent bar, and every audit file says which kind it is so the report can read it
- 2026-09-06 the first blind run (codex, node/calibration-audit) came back forty of forty and is refused unlanded: its packet's `diff` blocks were not diffs but sentences the same worker wrote after reading the ledger (`+ The command surface consolidated file listing into the list tool.`), which is the builder's reasoning handed to the auditor in a code fence. The check is reworded so blindness is a property a script can refuse: verbatim git hunks from the pinned corpus, a fresh session, and the packet re-derived at verify time
- 2026-09-06 cape-town, after the refusal: independence of information is derived by code and re-derived at verify time, never declared by an agent. Three checks above: the packet is code's alone and regenerated at verify; the auditor's transcript shows nothing but the packet; and the refused audit stays in the tree as a specimen the agreement script never reads. The specimen is in place already, so the next builder sees what a false blind looks like
- 2026-09-06 the mechanical blind run (codex, seed `calibration-audit-blind-2026-09-47`, packet sha256 d6791b87a99c9d35…, verbatim hunks from the pinned corpus) agreed on 9 of 20 blocked commits and 12 of 20 recall cases, under the bar, so the classification is untrusted and the verdict is pending again. Read case by case, the disagreement is mostly the packet's poverty rather than the ledger's: with rule ids and hunks alone the auditor judged whether a change was bad, not whether the rule's claim was true of it (it called an X1 hit on css class names a true positive as an injection risk, and every deleted test file a true positive without the replacement the builder had read), and on recall it found planted cases with no visible shape (a D1 case that only changed a version string, a T6 case that broke a test signature), which is a finding about the injector worth its own look. Shaped above as a fairness check: the packet carries what weeder itself printed, never what the builder wrote
- 2026-09-06 cape-town accepted the fairness redesign with one requirement, written into the check above: the packet carries the commit's full diff, every hunk, plus weeder's printed finding, so the auditor can see replacement coverage and judge whether the rule's claim is true of the change rather than whether the change is bad. The poverty diagnosis is a hypothesis and the fair packet is its test: still under the bar with a fair packet means the ledger is wrong and is redone
- 2026-09-06 the fairness node (codex) regenerated a fair packet, with catalogue text, weeder's findings, the planted site and the question, and kept the old response under it: the agreement table is still seed 47's 9 of 20 and 12 of 20, judged on the poor packet, and the transcript is a nineteen-line note saying a session happened. Two stamps refused. The evidence now demands the linkage a note cannot fake: the response declares the sha256 of the packet it answered and it has to be the fair packet's, and the transcript is the session's own record with the prompt and the verbatim answer. Seed 47 is spent; the fair run takes a fresh one
- 2026-09-06 the fair run (codex, two attempts) found the real limit: a packet of twenty full diffs and twenty recall cases is 60,000 lines, and the fresh session answered `Codex ran out of room in the model's context window`; a second attempt capped each section at 75 kB, got an answer in 92,000 input tokens, and was then refused at pleach's hygiene gate because a scratch copy of the packet under `.loop-scratch/` quoted the AWS documentation key from a sampled commit (dogfood, 2026-09-06). Reshaped above: one case, one file, one fresh session, one answer naming its file's hash; a diff past the generator's stated cap is reported as capped rather than cut. `scripts/trim-plan.sh` now tells workers where scratch goes, since the emitted prompt still says `.loop-scratch/` is never collected
- 2026-09-06 the per-case node (codex) closed with every check stamped and is refused a third time: its forty `sessions/*.events.jsonl` are two synthetic lines each, no codex thread or turn, the seed is still 47, and 31 of the 40 answers are the old response's reasoning verbatim. The conductor now runs the sessions: `scripts/audit/blind-run.sh <seed>` regenerates the case packets, hands each to a fresh `codex exec` in an empty directory with config and rules ignored, keeps the raw event stream as the record, and assembles the audit file from the answers; `audit-transcript.sh` refuses a record without a real thread, turn and one agent message. The generator, the case layout and the specimen from the node are kept
- 2026-09-06 the conductor's runner produced the first real blind re-grade: seed `calibration-audit-blind-2026-09-fair-1`, forty fresh `codex exec` sessions, no answer copied from any earlier run. Blocked commits 9 of 20 (six of the eleven disagreements are the auditor calling `false-positive` where the ledger says `acceptable` on T1 deletions whose cases moved, which is the finding's own sentence, `covered by nobody`, being untrue of the change; three are T2/S1 swaps between true-positive and acceptable; one is a capped diff the auditor could not see). Recall 12 of 20, with eight `not-a-case` answers, six of them D1 version-string plants and two T6 signature breaks, the injector defects recall now owns. Then the recall node, running at the same time, rewrote the campaign cache under `$TMPDIR` that the packet generator reads recall cases from, and thirteen recall packets stopped regenerating: the generator reads a cache, so the packet is only reproducible while nothing else touches it. Shaped above as re-planting from the pinned commit. The blocked half of this re-grade stands; the recall half is re-drawn once the injector lands
- 2026-09-06 the fair packets put the corpus's own hazards in weeder's tree: one spelled the AWS documentation key whole and carried a private-key fixture, so `tests/rule_x1.rs` and `tests/self_check.rs` went red on the packets' arrival. Two answers, both landed: the generator writes a published example as a named marker (`<published example credential, stamp AKIA>`), and the packets and session records live under `fixtures/adversarial/calibration-audit/`, the specimen root cape-town's ruling allows, where weeder reports them as notes. The session records still name the old path as their input, which the transcript evidence refuses until the next fair run writes new ones
- 2026-09-06 the calibration worker re-ran the blind sessions with `scripts/audit/blind-run.sh` on seed `calibration-audit-blind-2026-09-redo-2`, forty real `codex exec` records: blocked commits 14 of 20 against the redone ledger, recall cases 20 of 20 with the fixed injector. Sighted on the same draw, 40 of 40, which is the anchoring caveat measured rather than argued. Blocked agreement is under the bar, so the verdict stays qualified and the first sentence says the classification is untrusted; the six remaining disagreements are the acceptable-versus-true-positive line, where the auditor and the builder read the same true claim and disagree on whether the change weakened something
- 2026-09-06 the cache-independence check had been stamped by `audit-fairness.sh`, which never tests it. `scripts/check/packet-cache-free.sh` now derives the seed's packets twice, once from an empty `WEEDER_RECALL_CACHE` and once from this machine's, and five T6 recall packets differ: the replay of a recall case still reads something the campaign left behind. Open again, with the evidence that fails
- 2026-09-06 cape-town's ruling on the disputed line: a blind reader can judge whether the rule's claim is true of the change and nothing else, so the audited agreement on blocked commits is binary, claim-true or claim-false, and `acceptable` is a human label the audit never counts. Recorded in both audit files with the date before recomputing. On the responses already kept: seed fair-1 on the old ledger, 14 of 20 binary against 9 of 20 old-class; seed redo-2 on the redone ledger, 17 of 20 binary against 12 of 20 old-class, both runs. The three binary disagreements were the ledger calling claim-false what the ruling's own definition calls claim-true (assertions that really dropped from a file and moved elsewhere in the diff), so those three ledger calls are redone under the ruling and the message's consequence clause goes to rules-tests as T2's overclaim
- 2026-09-06 under the binary the kept responses agree: seed redo-2, blocked 20 of 20 (12 of 20 under the old classes, printed beside), recall 19 of 20; the sighted re-grade re-taken by `scripts/audit/sighted-run.sh` on the same draw, 20 of 20 both ways. The bar is read on the blind file alone
- 2026-09-06 after the T2 fix moved the block set from 23 to 20, both re-grades were re-taken by script on seed `calibration-audit-blind-2026-09-t2-1`: blind 19 of 20 blocked commits and 20 of 20 recall cases, sighted 20 of 20 both ways. The verdict stands unqualified on the blind file
- 2026-09-06 correcting the recall section moved the seeded sample by exactly one case: `recall-t6-ts-tend2-56072cdab` out, `recall-t2-py-copeca-70d669542` in, with the other 39 packets byte-identical and their seals intact. The blind half was repaired with one fresh auditor session on the new packet, which came back `miss` on its own. The sighted half needed more: its answers open with the SHA-256 of the report they were handed, and no check ever read that back, so every one of them had gone on naming a revision of `docs/calibration-2026-09.md` that no longer existed. The whole sighted half was re-run against the corrected report, and `audit-transcript.sh` now reads the anchor back and refuses a re-grade of a document that has changed under it. A hash nobody compares is decoration
- 2026-09-08 cape-town: the tokens rename with the tool, and the seal moves off the wording so the price is paid once. The packet the SHA covers becomes the judged content, rule id, level, path, line and the hunks; the sentence that teaches the token sits outside it, since the auditor's question is whether the rule's claim is true of the hunk. Forty fresh reads follow the rename; the calibration numbers do not move
- 2026-09-09 cape-town: codex is unusable on this account (a real session answers 404 on gpt-5.5), so the re-seal's blind reads run on opencode with deepseek-v4-pro, recorded with provider and model on every packet. A probe from the shell answers in a second with `opencode run --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --format json` reading the packet on stdin, and its record is step_start, text parts and step_finish events with a session id, which is what the transcript evidence reads for this population

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file — check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green — it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Probe/scratch files (toolchain checks, experiments) go in `.loop-scratch/` only — it is never collected; scratch files elsewhere pollute the delivery.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root — what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
